previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections, was admitted due to altered mental status, fever, and septic shock. He was found to have a severe E. coli urinary tract infection, leading to acute kidney injury and requiring ICU-level care initially. He was treated with intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam after culture confirmation, with improvement in infection markers and hemodynamic stability. A midline was placed for antibiotic administration, and his suprapubic catheter was exchanged. His baclofen pump was refilled and interrogated by pain management. Trazodone was initiated for insomnia with a normal follow-up EKG. He stabilized over eight days, completed necessary treatments, and was discharged to an extended care facility to finish his antibiotic course with follow-up coordinated through rehab.
